records.source: Λαλούντων δὲ αὐτῶν πρὸς τὸν λαὸν ἐπέστησαν αὐτοῖς οἱ ἱερεῖς καὶ ὁ στρατηγὸς τοῦ ἱεροῦ καὶ οἱ Σαδδουκαῖοι, διαπονούμενοι διὰ τὸ διδάσκειν αὐτοὺς τὸν λαὸν καὶ καταγγέλλειν ἐν τῷ Ἰησοῦ τὴν ἀνάστασιν τὴν ἐκ νεκρῶν, καὶ ἐπέβαλον αὐτοῖς τὰς χεῖρας καὶ ἔθεντο εἰς τήρησιν εἰς τὴν αὔριον, ἦν γὰρ ἑσπέρα ἤδη.
records.gloss: Speaking now of them to the people came upon them the priests and the captain of the temple and the Sadducees, \v 2 being greatly annoyed because of the to teach them the people and to proclaim in the Jesus the resurrection the from [the] dead, \v 3 and they laid on them the hands and put [them] into custody until the next day; it was for evening already.
pieces: Peter and John were still speaking to the people when the priests, the commander of the temple guard and the Sadducees confronted them.
These men were deeply irritated that the apostles were teaching the people and declaring that in Jesus there is resurrection from the dead.
They took hold of them and, because evening had already come, kept them under guard until the next day.

L.1: And while they were speaking to the people, the priests and the captain of the temple and the Sadducees came upon them,
L.2: being greatly annoyed because they were teaching the people and proclaiming in Jesus the resurrection from [the] dead.
L.3: And they laid hands on them and put [them] in custody until the next day, for it was already evening.

R.1: Peter and John were still talking to the people when some priests came up to them. The captain of the temple guards and some Sadducees came too.
R.2: They were very angry, because the apostles were teaching the people that because of Jesus, dead people will rise to life again.
R.3: So they grabbed Peter and John. It was already evening, so they put them in jail until the next day.

decisions.choice: the captain of the temple: the priest in command of the temple guard
decisions.reason: He was a senior priest who kept order in the temple courts with a force of Levites. Luke mentions such officers again in Luke 22:4 and Acts 5:24-26.

decisions.choice: the Sadducees: a party of the priestly upper class who denied the resurrection
decisions.reason: Luke says they held that there is no resurrection, nor angel, nor spirit (Luke 20:27; Acts 23:8). That explains their anger at what the apostles taught.

decisions.choice: in Jesus: Jesus's own rising shows, and brings about, the resurrection of the dead
alternatives: only that the dead rise through him
decisions.reason: The phrase can mean "in the case of Jesus" or "by means of Jesus". Both may be in view: his resurrection is the first, and others follow through him (compare 26:23; 1 Corinthians 15:20-22).

decisions.choice: greatly annoyed: deeply irritated
decisions.reason: The verb means to be worn out and provoked by something (16:18).

decisions.choice: until the next day: too late for a hearing
decisions.reason: It was evening, so the hearing was put off to the morning (4:5). The custody was a holding until then, not a punishment.

decisions.choice: the commander of the temple guard
decisions.reason: Balanced says what the officer commanded; Literal keeps the title.

decisions.choice: because of Jesus, dead people will rise to life again
alternatives: in Jesus the resurrection from the dead
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the sense that the resurrection comes through Jesus, as the meaning note explains.

records.heading: Peter and John taken into custody

records.source: πολλοὶ δὲ τῶν ἀκουσάντων τὸν λόγον ἐπίστευσαν, καὶ ἐγενήθη ὁ ἀριθμὸς τῶν ἀνδρῶν ὡς χιλιάδες πέντε.
records.gloss: Many however of those having heard the word believed, and became the number of the men about thousands five.
pieces: Even so, many who heard the message came to believe, and the count of men rose to about 5,000.

L.4: But many of those who had heard the word believed, and the number of the men came to about 5,000.

R.4: But many of the people who heard the message believed in Jesus. Now there were about 5,000 men who believed.

decisions.choice: the word: the message about Jesus
decisions.reason: As in 2:41, "the word" is the message the apostles preached.

decisions.choice: men: adult males
decisions.reason: The word usually means males, and Luke may count the men only, as in Luke 9:14. It can also stand for people in general, so the number may include women.

decisions.choice: the number: the whole number of believers now
alternatives: the number who believed that day
decisions.reason: The verb means that the number came to this total. Added to the 3,000 of 2:41 and those added daily (2:47), the whole community now reached about 5,000 men.

decisions.choice: believed in Jesus; men who believed
decisions.reason: Readable says in whom they believed, and that the count is of believers.

records.source: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐπὶ τὴν αὔριον συναχθῆναι αὐτῶν τοὺς ἄρχοντας καὶ τοὺς πρεσβυτέρους καὶ τοὺς γραμματεῖς ἐν Ἰερουσαλήμ καὶ Ἅννας ὁ ἀρχιερεὺς καὶ Καϊάφας καὶ Ἰωάννης καὶ Ἀλέξανδρος καὶ ὅσοι ἦσαν ἐκ γένους ἀρχιερατικοῦ, καὶ στήσαντες αὐτοὺς ἐν τῷ μέσῳ ἐπυνθάνοντο· Ἐν ποίᾳ δυνάμει ἢ ἐν ποίῳ ὀνόματι ἐποιήσατε τοῦτο ὑμεῖς;
records.gloss: It came to pass then on the next day were gathered of them the rulers and the elders and the scribes in Jerusalem, \v 6 and Annas the high priest and Caiaphas and John and Alexander and as many as were of family high-priestly, \v 7 and having set them in the midst they were inquiring, By what power or in what name did this you?
pieces: The next day the people's rulers, elders and experts in the law met together in Jerusalem.
Annas the high priest was there, with Caiaphas, John, Alexander and all the others from the high priest's family.
They had the two men stand in the center of the gathering and began questioning them: "What sort of power, or what sort of name, did you use to do this?"

L.5: And it came about on the next day that their rulers and elders and scribes were gathered together in Jerusalem,
L.6: and Annas the high priest and Caiaphas and John and Alexander, and as many as were of high-priestly descent.
L.7: And having set them in the middle, they began to inquire, "By what power or in what name did you do this?"

R.5: The next day the Jewish rulers, the elders and the teachers of the law met in Jerusalem.
R.6: Annas the high priest was there. Caiaphas, John, Alexander and the other men from the high priest's family were there too.
R.7: They made Peter and John stand in front of them. Then they asked, "How did you heal this man? What power did you use? Whose name did you use?"

decisions.choice: rulers, elders and scribes: the members of the Jewish high council
decisions.reason: These groups together made up the council in Jerusalem (4:15; Luke 22:66). "Their" means the rulers of the Jewish people.

decisions.choice: Annas the high priest, and Caiaphas
alternatives: Annas was the high priest in office
decisions.reason: Annas had been high priest years before and kept the title and great influence. His son-in-law Caiaphas held the office at this time (Luke 3:2; John 18:13).

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "John"
decisions.reason: One important manuscript, Codex Bezae, has "Jonathan", the name of a son of Annas who later became high priest. Most manuscripts have "John". Neither John nor Alexander is otherwise known. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: you: placed last, with weight
decisions.reason: The pronoun is written out and stands at the end, so it is stressed: men like you. It may carry scorn, which suits 4:13, but it may only point to them.

decisions.choice: this: the healing of the lame man
decisions.reason: Peter takes it so in 4:9.

decisions.choice: experts in the law; teachers of the law
decisions.reason: Scribes were scholars of the law of Moses; Balanced and Readable say so, and Literal keeps "scribes".

decisions.choice: How did you heal this man?
decisions.reason: Readable names what "this" refers to.

records.heading: No other name under heaven

records.source: τότε Πέτρος πλησθεὶς πνεύματος ἁγίου εἶπεν πρὸς αὐτούς· Ἄρχοντες τοῦ λαοῦ καὶ πρεσβύτεροι, εἰ ἡμεῖς σήμερον ἀνακρινόμεθα ἐπὶ εὐεργεσίᾳ ἀνθρώπου ἀσθενοῦς, ἐν τίνι οὗτος σέσωσται, γνωστὸν ἔστω πᾶσιν ὑμῖν καὶ παντὶ τῷ λαῷ Ἰσραὴλ ὅτι ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ τοῦ Ναζωραίου, ὃν ὑμεῖς ἐσταυρώσατε, ὃν ὁ θεὸς ἤγειρεν ἐκ νεκρῶν, ἐν τούτῳ οὗτος παρέστηκεν ἐνώπιον ὑμῶν ὑγιής.
records.gloss: Then Peter having been filled with [the] Spirit Holy said to them, Rulers of the people and elders, \v 9 if we today are being examined on a good deed of a man sick, by what this [man] has been saved, \v 10 known let it be to all you and to all the people of Israel that in the name of Jesus Christ the Nazarene, whom you crucified, whom the God raised from [the] dead, in this [one] this [man] stands before you healthy.
pieces: Then Peter, filled with the Holy Spirit, said to them, "Leaders of the people and elders,
since we are being questioned today about a kindness done for a disabled man, and how he was made well,

then all of you, and the whole people of Israel, must understand this. It was done in the name of Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} of Nazareth, whom you crucified and whom God raised from the dead. Through {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} this man is standing in front of you, sound and whole.

L.8: Then Peter, filled with [the] Holy Spirit, said to them, "Rulers of the people and elders,
L.9: if we are being examined today concerning a good deed [done] to a sick man, by what means this [man] has been made well,
L.10: let it be known to all of you and to all the people of Israel that in the name of Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} the Nazarene, whom you crucified, whom God raised from [the] dead, in this [one] this [man] stands before you healthy.

R.8: Then the Holy Spirit filled Peter, and he said to them, "Leaders and elders of the people,
R.9: today you are asking us about something good we did for a man who could not walk. You want to know how he was made well.
R.10: All of you, and all the people of Israel, need to know this. This man was healed by the power of Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}} from Nazareth. You nailed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to a cross, but God brought {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} back to life. Because of Jesus, this man is standing here in front of you, completely well.

decisions.choice: filled with the Holy Spirit: given the Spirit's power for this moment
decisions.reason: Jesus promised that when his followers were brought before rulers, the Holy Spirit would teach them what to say (Luke 12:11-12, 21:12-15). The verb looks at a filling for the task at hand.

decisions.choice: if: since, as is in fact the case
decisions.reason: The condition is stated as true: they are being examined.

decisions.choice: has been made well: healed, and also saved
decisions.reason: The verb means to save or to make well. Peter uses the healing to lead to the salvation that comes only through Jesus (4:12).

decisions.choice: in this one: by Jesus, or by this name
decisions.reason: The word can refer to Jesus or to his name. The meaning hardly differs, since the name stands for the person. Literal keeps the open form.

decisions.choice: in the name of Jesus: by his authority and power
decisions.reason: As at 3:6 and 3:16.

decisions.choice: since
decisions.reason: Balanced shows that the condition is true, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: by the power of
decisions.reason: As at 3:6, Readable says what the name means here.

records.source: οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ λίθος ὁ ἐξουθενηθεὶς ὑφ’ ὑμῶν τῶν οἰκοδόμων, ὁ γενόμενος εἰς κεφαλὴν γωνίας.
records.gloss: This is the stone the having been despised by you the builders, the having become into head of corner.
pieces: He is the stone that you builders scorned as worthless, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has become the head of the corner.

L.11: This [one] is the stone that was despised by you, the builders, which has become [the] head of [the] corner.

R.11: Jesus is like the stone that the builders threw away as useless. But that stone has now become the most important stone in the building.

decisions.choice: the rejected stone: Psalm 118:22
decisions.reason: Peter takes the words of Psalm 118:22 and applies them to his hearers: "you, the builders". Jesus used the same verse of himself (Luke 20:17). Because Peter changes the wording, it is not set off as a quotation.

decisions.choice: despised: treated as worth nothing
decisions.reason: Peter uses a stronger word than the psalm's "rejected": the builders held the stone in contempt.

decisions.choice: head of the corner: the stone that holds the building together
decisions.reason: The phrase may mean the main cornerstone of the foundation or the top stone that completes an arch or wall. Either way it is the most important stone.

decisions.choice: Jesus is like the stone
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus and marks the picture as a comparison.

records.source: καὶ οὐκ ἔστιν ἐν ἄλλῳ οὐδενὶ ἡ σωτηρία, οὐδὲ γὰρ ὄνομά ἐστιν ἕτερον ὑπὸ τὸν οὐρανὸν τὸ δεδομένον ἐν ἀνθρώποις ἐν ᾧ δεῖ σωθῆναι ἡμᾶς.
records.gloss: And not there is in other no one the salvation, not for name is another under the heaven the having been given among men in which it is necessary to be saved us.
pieces: Salvation comes through no one but {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Under all of heaven God has given humankind no other name through which we are to be saved."

L.12: And there is salvation in no one else, for neither is there another name under heaven that has been given among {{gender:people|men}} by which we must be saved."

R.12: Only Jesus can bring salvation. In the whole world God has not given us anyone else who can save us. We must be saved by {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}."

decisions.choice: salvation: rescue from sin and death, the whole of what God saves people for
decisions.reason: The man's healing ("made well", 4:9) is a sign of a greater salvation that comes only through Jesus (2:21, 2:40).

decisions.choice: name: the person who bears it
decisions.reason: As in 4:10, the name stands for Jesus himself.

decisions.choice: under heaven: anywhere in the world
decisions.reason: The phrase means everywhere people live (2:5).

decisions.choice: we must be saved: it is God's will that salvation come this way
alternatives: we are forced to be saved
decisions.reason: The word for "must" often expresses God's plan in Luke's writings (Luke 24:26; Acts 1:16, 3:21).

decisions.choice: men: human beings
decisions.reason: The word means people in general.

decisions.choice: God has given
decisions.reason: The passive means that God gave the name; Balanced and Readable say so.

decisions.choice: people, with "men" as the alternative
decisions.reason: The word means human beings, men and women.

records.source: Θεωροῦντες δὲ τὴν τοῦ Πέτρου παρρησίαν καὶ Ἰωάννου καὶ καταλαβόμενοι ὅτι ἄνθρωποι ἀγράμματοί εἰσιν καὶ ἰδιῶται, ἐθαύμαζον, ἐπεγίνωσκόν τε αὐτοὺς ὅτι σὺν τῷ Ἰησοῦ ἦσαν, τόν τε ἄνθρωπον βλέποντες σὺν αὐτοῖς ἑστῶτα τὸν τεθεραπευμένον οὐδὲν εἶχον ἀντειπεῖν.
records.gloss: Seeing now the of the Peter boldness and of John, and having perceived that men unlettered they are and untrained, they were marveling, they were recognizing and them that with the Jesus they had been; \v 14 the and man seeing with them standing, the having been healed, nothing they had to say against.
pieces: The council members saw how freely Peter and John spoke, and they realized these were men without formal schooling, just ordinary people. This astonished them, and they recognized that the two had been companions of Jesus.
But with the healed man standing right there beside them, they could say nothing to refute it.

L.13: Now seeing the boldness of Peter and John, and having perceived that they were unlettered and untrained men, they were amazed, and they recognized them, that they had been with Jesus.
L.14: And seeing the man who had been healed standing with them, they had nothing to say against [it].

R.13: The leaders saw that Peter and John were not afraid to speak. They also knew that these men had never studied the law in school. They were just ordinary men. So the leaders were amazed. They also realized that Peter and John had been with Jesus.
R.14: The man who had been healed was standing there with them. So the leaders could not say anything against what had happened.

decisions.choice: boldness: frank, fearless speech
decisions.reason: The word means speaking openly and without fear. It returns in the prayer (4:29) and its answer (4:31).

decisions.choice: unlettered: without training in the law
decisions.reason: The word can mean illiterate, but here it means they had not studied the Scriptures under a recognized teacher (compare John 7:15).

decisions.choice: untrained: ordinary people, not professionals
decisions.reason: The word means a private person, a layman without special skill.

decisions.choice: they recognized: they saw them for what they were, men who had been with Jesus
alternatives: they now remembered seeing them with Jesus
decisions.reason: The verb can mean to recognize faces or to come to understand. Either way, the council saw that the apostles' boldness came from having been with Jesus.

decisions.choice: the council members; the leaders
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name who saw this.

records.heading: We cannot stop speaking

records.source: κελεύσαντες δὲ αὐτοὺς ἔξω τοῦ συνεδρίου ἀπελθεῖν συνέβαλλον πρὸς ἀλλήλους λέγοντες· Τί ποιήσωμεν τοῖς ἀνθρώποις τούτοις;
records.gloss: Having commanded however them outside the Council to go away, they were conferring with one another \v 16 saying, What shall we do to the men these?
pieces: So they ordered them to step out of the council room, and then they talked the matter over among themselves.
They said, "What can we do with these men?

L.15: But having ordered them to go outside the Council, they began conferring with one another,
L.16: saying, "What shall we do with these men?

R.15: So they told Peter and John to go out of the room where the council met. Then the leaders talked together.
R.16: They said, "What should we do with these men?

decisions.choice: the Council: the Sanhedrin, the high council of the Jewish people in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The word can mean the council itself or the hall where it met. Here the apostles leave the meeting.

decisions.choice: what shall we do: a real question, asking what is possible
decisions.reason: The council is at a loss, as the next words show.

decisions.choice: the council room; the room where the council met
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say where the apostles were sent from.

records.source: ὅτι μὲν γὰρ γνωστὸν σημεῖον γέγονεν δι’ αὐτῶν πᾶσιν τοῖς κατοικοῦσιν Ἰερουσαλὴμ φανερόν, καὶ οὐ δυνάμεθα ἀρνεῖσθαι·
records.gloss: That indeed for a known sign has come about through them to all those inhabiting Jerusalem [is] evident, and not we are able to deny [it].
pieces: A remarkable sign has clearly been done through them; the whole population of Jerusalem can see it, and there is no way we can say it did not happen.

L.16: For that a notable sign has come about through them is evident to all who live in Jerusalem, and we cannot deny [it].

R.16: Everyone in Jerusalem knows about this amazing sign. It is clear that it happened through them, and we cannot say that it did not happen.

decisions.choice: sign: a miracle that points to God's power and purpose
decisions.reason: Luke calls the healing a sign in 4:22 and 4:30, as in 2:22 and 2:43.

decisions.choice: notable: widely known and undeniable
decisions.reason: The word means known, and so plain to see.

decisions.choice: through them: they were the means, not the source
decisions.reason: The council speaks of the apostles as the ones through whom it happened, as Peter had insisted (3:12, 4:10).

decisions.choice: there is no way we can say it did not happen
decisions.reason: Balanced spells out what denying it would mean.

records.source: ἀλλ’ ἵνα μὴ ἐπὶ πλεῖον διανεμηθῇ εἰς τὸν λαόν, ἀπειλησώμεθα αὐτοῖς μηκέτι λαλεῖν ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματι τούτῳ μηδενὶ ἀνθρώπων.
records.gloss: But that not further it may spread among the people, let us threaten them no longer to speak on the name this to no one of men.
pieces: Still, this must not spread more widely among the people. Let us threaten them, so that they never again speak to anyone in this name."

L.17: But so that it may not spread further among the people, let us threaten them to speak no longer in this name to anyone."

R.17: But we must stop this from spreading to more people. Let us warn them strongly. They must never again speak to anyone in the name of this man."

decisions.choice: it may spread: the news of the healing and the message with it
decisions.reason: The subject is not stated. It is what has happened and what the apostles say about it.

decisions.choice: threaten: warn with the promise of punishment
decisions.reason: The verb means to threaten. The prayer of 4:29 asks God to look on these threats.

decisions.choice: this name: the name of Jesus, which the council avoids saying
decisions.reason: The leaders speak of "this name" without saying it. To speak "in" or "on" the name is to speak by Jesus's authority and about him.

decisions.choice: no longer ... to no one: a complete ban
decisions.reason: The double negative makes the ban total.

decisions.choice: anyone
decisions.reason: English has no smooth form for "no one of men"; Literal gives the sense.

decisions.choice: in the name of this man
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the leaders' refusal to say the name, as the meaning note explains.

records.source: καὶ καλέσαντες αὐτοὺς παρήγγειλαν τὸ καθόλου μὴ φθέγγεσθαι μηδὲ διδάσκειν ἐπὶ τῷ ὀνόματι τοῦ Ἰησοῦ.
records.gloss: And having called them they commanded the at all not to speak nor to teach in the name of the Jesus.
pieces: They called the two men back and gave them a strict order: they were not to speak or teach in the name of Jesus in any way at all.

L.18: And calling them, they commanded [them] not to speak or to teach at all in the name of Jesus.

R.18: Then they called Peter and John back into the room. They ordered them never to speak or teach in the name of Jesus at all.

decisions.choice: to speak: to say anything out loud
decisions.reason: The verb means to utter or speak out. The ban covers any speaking, not only formal teaching.

decisions.choice: not at all: the ban is total
decisions.reason: The word means entirely.

decisions.choice: in the name of Jesus: by his authority, and so about him
alternatives: using his name as a spell
decisions.reason: As in 4:17. Now the council says the name.

decisions.choice: called them back
decisions.reason: They had been sent out of the room (4:15), so Balanced and Readable say they were called back.

records.source: ὁ δὲ Πέτρος καὶ Ἰωάννης ἀποκριθέντες εἶπον πρὸς αὐτούς· Εἰ δίκαιόν ἐστιν ἐνώπιον τοῦ θεοῦ ὑμῶν ἀκούειν μᾶλλον ἢ τοῦ θεοῦ, κρίνατε, οὐ δυνάμεθα γὰρ ἡμεῖς ἃ εἴδαμεν καὶ ἠκούσαμεν μὴ λαλεῖν.
records.gloss: The but Peter and John answering said to them, Whether right it is before the God you to listen to rather than the God, judge; \v 20 not are able for we what we saw and heard not to speak.
pieces: But Peter and John answered them, "You must decide whether, in God's sight, it is right to heed you rather than God.
For our part, we cannot stay silent about the things we have seen and heard."

L.19: But Peter and John answered and said to them, "Whether it is right before God to listen to you rather than to God, you judge,
L.20: for we cannot but speak what we have seen and heard."

R.19: But Peter and John answered, "What does God think is right? Should we obey you, or should we obey God? You decide!
R.20: We cannot stop talking about what we have seen and heard."

decisions.choice: to listen to: to obey
decisions.reason: To listen to someone in this sense is to do what they say. Peter says the same thing more sharply in 5:29.

decisions.choice: before God: in God's judgment
decisions.reason: The question is how God sees the matter.

decisions.choice: you judge: a challenge to the council
decisions.reason: The apostles leave the answer to the judges themselves, knowing it can only be one way.

decisions.choice: we cannot not speak: we must speak
alternatives: we are not allowed to speak
decisions.reason: The two negatives make a strong positive: they are bound to tell what they saw and heard, as witnesses (1:8).

decisions.choice: two questions and a command
decisions.reason: Readable breaks Peter's challenge into short sentences.

records.source: οἱ δὲ προσαπειλησάμενοι ἀπέλυσαν αὐτούς, μηδὲν εὑρίσκοντες τὸ πῶς κολάσωνται αὐτούς, διὰ τὸν λαόν, ὅτι πάντες ἐδόξαζον τὸν θεὸν ἐπὶ τῷ γεγονότι·
records.gloss: They and having further threatened released them, nothing finding the how they might punish them, because of the people, because all were glorifying the God for the having happened.
pieces: The council threatened them still more and then set them free. They could see no way to punish them because of the people, who were all giving glory to God for what had happened.

L.21: And having threatened [them] further, they released them, finding no way how they might punish them, because of the people, for all were glorifying God for what had happened.

R.21: The leaders threatened them even more and then let them go. They could not find a way to punish them, because they were afraid of what the people would do. All the people were giving glory to God because of what had happened.

decisions.choice: having threatened further: adding threats to the order
decisions.reason: The verb means to threaten in addition, on top of the command of 4:18.

decisions.choice: because of the people: the council feared the crowd
decisions.reason: The council had to reckon with the people, who were on the apostles' side (compare 5:26; Luke 22:2).

decisions.choice: glorifying God: praising God and giving him honor
decisions.reason: The people gave the credit to God.

decisions.choice: because they were afraid of what the people would do
decisions.reason: Readable says why the people mattered, as the meaning note explains.

records.source: ἐτῶν γὰρ ἦν πλειόνων τεσσεράκοντα ὁ ἄνθρωπος ἐφ’ ὃν γεγόνει τὸ σημεῖον τοῦτο τῆς ἰάσεως.
records.gloss: Of years for was more than forty the man on whom had happened the sign this of the healing.
pieces: This sign of healing had happened to a man more than forty years old.

L.22: For the man on whom this sign of healing had come about was more than forty years old.

R.22: The man who was healed by this sign was more than forty years old. He had not been able to walk for his whole life.

decisions.choice: for: this explains why everyone gave glory to God
decisions.reason: A man lame from birth for over forty years (3:2) could not be healed by any ordinary means.

decisions.choice: this sign of healing: the healing was itself the sign
alternatives: a sign that went with the healing
decisions.reason: The healing points to God's power at work through Jesus (4:16, 4:30).

decisions.choice: He had not been able to walk for his whole life
decisions.reason: Readable repeats from 3:2 why his age mattered.

records.source: Ἀπολυθέντες δὲ ἦλθον πρὸς τοὺς ἰδίους καὶ ἀπήγγειλαν ὅσα πρὸς αὐτοὺς οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ πρεσβύτεροι εἶπαν.
records.gloss: Having been released now they came to the own and reported as much as to them the chief priests and the elders said.
pieces: As soon as they were set free, the two went back to their fellow believers and gave an account of everything the chief priests and elders had told them.

L.23: And having been released, they went to their own [people] and reported all that the chief priests and the elders had said to them.

R.23: After they were let go, Peter and John went back to the other believers. They told them everything the leading priests and elders had said.

decisions.choice: their own: their fellow believers
decisions.reason: The phrase means their own people. The prayer that follows is the prayer of a gathered group of believers (4:31).

decisions.choice: chief priests: the high priest and the leading priestly families
decisions.reason: The word covers the high priest, former high priests and the heads of the priestly families named in 4:6.

decisions.choice: fellow believers; the other believers
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say who "their own" were.

records.heading: The believers pray for boldness

records.source: οἱ δὲ ἀκούσαντες ὁμοθυμαδὸν ἦραν φωνὴν πρὸς τὸν θεὸν καὶ εἶπαν· Δέσποτα, σὺ ὁ ποιήσας τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ τὴν γῆν καὶ τὴν θάλασσαν καὶ πάντα τὰ ἐν αὐτοῖς, ὁ τοῦ πατρὸς ἡμῶν διὰ πνεύματος ἁγίου στόματος Δαυὶδ παιδός σου εἰπών· Ἱνατί ἐφρύαξαν ἔθνη καὶ λαοὶ ἐμελέτησαν κενά;
records.gloss: They and having heard with one accord lifted voice to the God and said, Master, you the having made the heaven and the earth and the sea and all the [things] in them, \v 25 the of the father of us through Spirit Holy mouth of David servant of you having said, Why did rage nations and peoples devised empty things?
pieces: When they heard it, they lifted their voices to God together and prayed: "Sovereign Master, maker of heaven and earth, of the sea, and of everything they hold!

It was {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} who spoke by the Holy Spirit through the mouth of our father David, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant: 'Why were the nations in an uproar, and why did the peoples scheme for nothing?

L.24: And having heard [it], with one mind they raised [their] voice to God and said, "Sovereign Master, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} [are] the one who made the heaven and the earth and the sea and all that is in them,
L.25: who through [the] Holy Spirit, by [the] mouth of our father David, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} servant, said, 'Why did [the] nations rage, and [the] peoples plot empty things?

R.24: When the believers heard this, they all prayed to God together. They said, "Master, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} made the sky, the earth, the sea and everything in them.
R.25: Long ago, by the Holy Spirit, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} spoke through our ancestor David, who served {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. You said, 'Why were the nations so angry? Why did the peoples make useless plans?

decisions.choice: Master: the sovereign owner and ruler
decisions.reason: This is not the usual word for Lord. It means the master of a household, with full authority over its slaves (compare 4:29). Luke 2:29 uses it of God in Simeon's prayer.

decisions.choice: the maker of heaven, earth and sea: the words of Exodus 20:11 and Psalm 146:6
decisions.reason: The believers address God as Creator in words from Israel's Scriptures, and so as the one who rules over every earthly power.

decisions.choice: SBLGNT: "who through the Holy Spirit, by the mouth of our father David your servant, said"
alternatives: many manuscripts read "who by the mouth of David your servant said"
decisions.reason: The Greek of this verse is notoriously awkward, and the manuscripts differ. Many later manuscripts, followed by the King James Version, lack "our father" and "through the Holy Spirit". The early manuscripts have the fuller, harder text that the SBLGNT prints. Reviewers should check this against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: Psalm 2:1-2: the nations against God and his anointed king
decisions.reason: The believers quote the Greek Old Testament word for word, running on into 4:26. The psalm is a royal psalm; Acts 13:33 quotes it again of Jesus.

decisions.choice: did rage ... plotted: past tense
decisions.reason: The verbs are past, and the prayer sees the psalm fulfilled in what had happened to Jesus (4:27).

decisions.choice: Sovereign Master
decisions.reason: "Master" keeps this word apart from the usual word for Lord (4:29); "Sovereign" shows that the master is God.

decisions.choice: our ancestor David
decisions.reason: Readable says what "father" means here. David is one named man, so there is no gender setting.

records.source: παρέστησαν οἱ βασιλεῖς τῆς γῆς καὶ οἱ ἄρχοντες συνήχθησαν ἐπὶ τὸ αὐτὸ κατὰ τοῦ κυρίου καὶ κατὰ τοῦ χριστοῦ αὐτοῦ.
records.gloss: Took their stand the kings of the earth and the rulers were gathered together on the same against the Lord and against the Christ of him.
pieces: The kings of the earth took up their positions, and the rulers joined forces against the Lord and against {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.'

L.26: The kings of the earth took their stand, and the rulers were gathered together against the Lord and against {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.'

R.26: The kings of the earth got ready to fight. The rulers came together to fight against the Lord and against {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, the King {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} chose.'

decisions.choice: the Lord: God, whose name is written in Psalm 2:2
decisions.reason: The Hebrew of Psalm 2:2 has the divine name, which the Greek translates "Lord".

decisions.choice: his anointed: the king God chose, and Jesus
decisions.reason: In the psalm the word is the anointed king of Israel. The believers see it fulfilled in Jesus, whom God anointed (4:27, 10:38).

decisions.choice: gathered together: assembled as one
alternatives: gathered to the same place only
decisions.reason: The phrase means together in one body; the same verb returns in 4:27.

decisions.choice: the King he chose
decisions.reason: Readable explains the title once.

records.source: συνήχθησαν γὰρ ἐπ’ ἀληθείας ἐν τῇ πόλει ταύτῃ ἐπὶ τὸν ἅγιον παῖδά σου Ἰησοῦν, ὃν ἔχρισας, Ἡρῴδης τε καὶ Πόντιος Πιλᾶτος σὺν ἔθνεσιν καὶ λαοῖς Ἰσραήλ, ποιῆσαι ὅσα ἡ χείρ σου καὶ ἡ βουλὴ προώρισεν γενέσθαι.
records.gloss: Were gathered together for in truth in the city this against the holy servant of you Jesus whom you anointed, Herod both and Pontius Pilate with nations and peoples of Israel, \v 28 to do as much as the hand of you and the plan of you predetermined to happen.
pieces: In truth, here in this very city, Herod and Pontius Pilate assembled with the nations and with the peoples of Israel against {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} holy servant Jesus, the one {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} anointed.
They carried out everything that {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} power and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} purpose had already settled must take place.

L.27: For in truth there were gathered together in this city against {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} holy servant Jesus, whom {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} anointed, both Herod and Pontius Pilate, with [the] nations and [the] peoples of Israel,
L.28: to do whatever {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hand and plan had determined beforehand would happen.

R.27: This is the truth: Herod and Pontius Pilate came together here in this city against Jesus, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} holy servant. You chose {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and anointed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} as King. The people of other nations and the people of Israel joined them against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
R.28: They did what {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} power had already planned. You had decided long ago that these things would happen.

decisions.choice: in truth: truly, as the psalm said
decisions.reason: The phrase means "indeed". It marks the events in Jerusalem as the real fulfillment of the psalm.

decisions.choice: Herod and Pontius Pilate: the king and the Roman governor at Jesus's trial
decisions.reason: Herod Antipas, ruler of Galilee, and Pilate, governor of Judea, both questioned Jesus (Luke 23:1-12). They stand for the psalm's "kings" and "rulers"; the nations and the peoples of Israel stand for its "nations" and "peoples".

decisions.choice: servant: the servant of God, as in Isaiah
decisions.reason: As at 3:13 and 3:26.

decisions.choice: your hand and your plan determined beforehand: God's power and purpose ruled the events
decisions.reason: The verb means to decide in advance. The same thought is in 2:23. Those who acted against Jesus were still responsible (2:23, 3:13-15).

decisions.choice: your hand: your power
decisions.reason: In the Scriptures God's hand is his power at work.

decisions.choice: your power
decisions.reason: Balanced says what the picture means; Literal keeps it. 4:30 keeps "hand" at Balanced, where the picture of stretching it out matters.

decisions.choice: chose him and anointed him as King
decisions.reason: Readable says what anointing meant, linking it to the King of 4:26.

records.source: καὶ τὰ νῦν, κύριε, ἔπιδε ἐπὶ τὰς ἀπειλὰς αὐτῶν καὶ δὸς τοῖς δούλοις σου μετὰ παρρησίας πάσης λαλεῖν τὸν λόγον σου, ἐν τῷ τὴν χεῖρά σου ἐκτείνειν σε εἰς ἴασιν καὶ σημεῖα καὶ τέρατα γίνεσθαι διὰ τοῦ ὀνόματος τοῦ ἁγίου παιδός σου Ἰησοῦ.
records.gloss: And the now, Lord, look upon the threats of them and grant to the slaves of you with boldness all to speak the word of you, \v 30 in the the hand of you to stretch out you for healing and signs and wonders to happen through the name of the holy servant of you Jesus.
pieces: Now, Lord, take notice of their threats. Let {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} slaves speak {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} word with complete boldness,
while {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} put out {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hand to heal, and signs and wonders are done through the name of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} holy servant Jesus."

L.29: And now, Lord, look upon their threats, and grant to {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} slaves to speak {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} word with all boldness,
L.30: while {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} stretch out {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hand for healing, and signs and wonders take place through the name of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} holy servant Jesus."

R.29: Now, Lord, see how they are threatening us. Help us, {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} slaves, to speak {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} message bravely.
R.30: Show {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} power and heal people. Let signs and wonders happen by the power of the name of {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} holy servant Jesus."

decisions.choice: Lord: God, to whom the prayer is made
decisions.reason: The prayer is addressed to God (4:24), who is asked to act through "your holy servant Jesus".

decisions.choice: slaves: people who belong wholly to their master
decisions.reason: The word means a slave, owned by a master. It answers "Master" in 4:24: the believers belong to God and serve him alone.

decisions.choice: while you stretch out your hand: God's acts go with their speaking
decisions.reason: The construction means "as" or "by": they ask for boldness to speak as God works with power.

decisions.choice: to stretch out your hand: to act with power
decisions.reason: The picture is used of God's mighty acts at the exodus (Exodus 3:20, 6:6).

decisions.choice: signs and wonders: miracles that point to God and cause awe
slaves
decisions.reason: "Slave" at every level: "servant" already renders a different word for Jesus, "your holy servant", in the same sentence (verse 30), so the style guide keeps the two words distinct (m2).

decisions.choice: threatening us; help us, your slaves
decisions.reason: Readable lets the believers speak of themselves; the threats were made against Peter and John.

records.source: καὶ δεηθέντων αὐτῶν ἐσαλεύθη ὁ τόπος ἐν ᾧ ἦσαν συνηγμένοι, καὶ ἐπλήσθησαν ἅπαντες τοῦ ἁγίου πνεύματος, καὶ ἐλάλουν τὸν λόγον τοῦ θεοῦ μετὰ παρρησίας.
records.gloss: And having prayed of them was shaken the place in which they were gathered together, and they were filled all of the Holy Spirit and were speaking the word of the God with boldness.
pieces: When they finished praying, the place where they had met shook, and every one of them was filled with the Holy Spirit, and they went on proclaiming God's word fearlessly.

L.31: And when they had prayed, the place in which they were gathered together was shaken, and they were all filled with the Holy Spirit and were speaking the word of God with boldness.

R.31: After they prayed, the place where they were meeting shook. The Holy Spirit filled all of them. Then they told God's message to people, and they were not afraid.

decisions.choice: the place was shaken: a sign that God had heard
decisions.reason: In the Scriptures the earth shakes when God comes near (Exodus 19:18; Isaiah 6:4). Here it answers the prayer.

decisions.choice: filled with the Holy Spirit: given the Spirit's power again
alternatives: receiving the Spirit for the first time
decisions.reason: Those who had been filled at Pentecost (2:4) were filled again for the task at hand, as Peter was (4:8).

decisions.choice: were speaking with boldness: from then on they kept speaking
decisions.reason: The verb is in the imperfect: they went on speaking. It answers what they asked in 4:29.

decisions.choice: fearlessly
decisions.reason: Balanced varies the wording; the meaning is the same boldness as in 4:13 and 4:29.

records.source: Τοῦ δὲ πλήθους τῶν πιστευσάντων ἦν καρδία καὶ ψυχὴ μία, καὶ οὐδὲ εἷς τι τῶν ὑπαρχόντων αὐτῷ ἔλεγεν ἴδιον εἶναι, ἀλλ’ ἦν αὐτοῖς πάντα κοινά.
records.gloss: Of the and multitude of those having believed was heart and soul one, and not even one anything of the possessions to him was saying own to be, but were to them all things common.
pieces: The whole company of believers shared a single heart and soul. Not one of them treated anything they owned as theirs alone; everything they had belonged to them all.

L.32: And the multitude of those who had believed were of one heart and soul, and not even one [of them] said that anything of what they possessed was their own, but all things were common to them.

R.32: All the believers agreed with each other in what they thought and what they wanted. None of them said, "This belongs only to me." Instead, they shared everything they had.

decisions.choice: one heart and soul: one in mind and will
decisions.reason: Heart and soul together mean the whole inner person. They were united in what they thought and what they wanted.

decisions.choice: said that nothing was his own: no one held back what he owned
decisions.reason: They still owned things (4:34, 5:4), but none of them claimed a right to keep anything from the others.

decisions.choice: all things in common: as in 2:44
decisions.reason: Luke repeats what he said in 2:44. Greek writers had a saying that friends hold all things in common; here it was so in practice.

decisions.choice: a quoted saying
alternatives: not one said that anything was his own
decisions.reason: Readable turns what no one said into words no one spoke.

records.heading: One heart and soul

records.source: καὶ δυνάμει μεγάλῃ ἀπεδίδουν τὸ μαρτύριον οἱ ἀπόστολοι τῆς ἀναστάσεως τοῦ κυρίου Ἰησοῦ, χάρις τε μεγάλη ἦν ἐπὶ πάντας αὐτούς.
records.gloss: And with power great were giving the testimony the apostles of the resurrection of the Lord Jesus, grace and great was upon all them.
pieces: With mighty power the apostles went on declaring that the Lord Jesus had risen, and God's grace rested richly on them all.

L.33: And with great power the apostles kept bearing witness to the resurrection of the Lord Jesus, and great grace was upon all of them.

R.33: With great power the apostles kept telling people that the Lord Jesus had come back to life. And God's grace was strongly at work in all the believers.

decisions.choice: great power: God's power, in their words and in miracles
decisions.reason: Power in Acts is the Spirit's power promised in 1:8, seen in bold witness and in signs (4:30, 5:12).

decisions.choice: grace: God's favor and kindness at work in them
decisions.reason: In 2:47 the believers had favor with all the people, and the word could mean that here. But nothing is said here about the people, and the next verse speaks of what God's kindness did among them. So it is God's grace.

decisions.choice: them all: the whole community of believers
decisions.reason: The verse moves from the apostles to all of them, and 4:34 goes on to speak of the whole community.

decisions.choice: God's grace
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say whose grace it is, as the meaning note explains.

decisions.choice: all the believers
decisions.reason: Readable says who "all" were.

records.source: οὐδὲ γὰρ ἐνδεής τις ἦν ἐν αὐτοῖς· ὅσοι γὰρ κτήτορες χωρίων ἢ οἰκιῶν ὑπῆρχον, πωλοῦντες ἔφερον τὰς τιμὰς τῶν πιπρασκομένων καὶ ἐτίθουν παρὰ τοὺς πόδας τῶν ἀποστόλων· διεδίδετο δὲ ἑκάστῳ καθότι ἄν τις χρείαν εἶχεν.
records.gloss: Not even for in need anyone was among them; as many as for owners of lands or of houses were, selling were bringing the prices of the [things] being sold \v 35 and were laying at the feet of the apostles; was distributed and to each according as anyone need had.
pieces: No one among them lacked anything, since any who owned fields or houses would sell them and bring what the sale had raised.
They laid it at the apostles' feet, and it was shared out to each person as each one had need.

L.34: For there was not even anyone in need among them, for as many as were owners of lands or houses, selling [them], would bring the proceeds of what was sold
L.35: and lay [them] at the feet of the apostles, and it was distributed to each as anyone had need.

R.34: None of the believers needed anything. Some of them owned land or houses. They sold these things and brought the money.
R.35: They gave it to the apostles. Then the apostles gave the money to anyone who needed it.

decisions.choice: not anyone in need: Deuteronomy 15:4
decisions.reason: God told Israel that if they obeyed him there would be no poor among them (Deuteronomy 15:4). The words are close to the Greek of that verse.

decisions.choice: would sell ... would bring ... would lay: done again and again as needs arose
decisions.reason: The verbs are in the imperfect and describe repeated action, not one sale of everything.

decisions.choice: at the feet of the apostles: placed in their charge
alternatives: a gift to the apostles themselves
decisions.reason: Laying something at a person's feet hands it over to their authority. The apostles then gave it out to those in need.

decisions.choice: lands: fields or plots of land
decisions.reason: The word means a piece of land, such as a field.

decisions.choice: gave it to the apostles
alternatives: laid it at the apostles' feet
decisions.reason: Readable says what the gesture meant, as the meaning note explains.

records.source: Ἰωσὴφ δὲ ὁ ἐπικληθεὶς Βαρναβᾶς ἀπὸ τῶν ἀποστόλων, ὅ ἐστιν μεθερμηνευόμενον υἱὸς παρακλήσεως, Λευίτης, Κύπριος τῷ γένει, ὑπάρχοντος αὐτῷ ἀγροῦ πωλήσας ἤνεγκεν τὸ χρῆμα καὶ ἔθηκεν παρὰ τοὺς πόδας τῶν ἀποστόλων.
records.gloss: Joseph now the having been called Barnabas by the apostles, which is being translated Son of encouragement, a Levite, a Cypriot by the birth, \v 37 belonging to him a field, having sold brought the money and laid at the feet of the apostles.
pieces: One of them was Joseph, a Levite born in Cyprus, to whom the apostles gave the name Barnabas, meaning "one who encourages."
He sold a field that he owned, then brought the money and set it down at the apostles' feet.

L.36: And Joseph, who was called Barnabas by the apostles (which is translated Son of Encouragement), a Levite, a Cypriot by birth,
L.37: having a field, sold [it] and brought the money and laid [it] at the feet of the apostles.

R.36: One of the believers was a man named Joseph. He was a Levite, and he was born on the island of Cyprus. The apostles called him Barnabas. That name means "someone who encourages others."
R.37: Joseph owned a field. He sold it, brought the money and gave it to the apostles.

decisions.choice: son of encouragement: one who encourages
alternatives: the son of a man named Encouragement
decisions.reason: "Son of" a quality describes a person's character. Barnabas lives up to the name (11:23). How the name gives this meaning is not certain; the word translated "encouragement" can also mean comfort or exhortation.

decisions.choice: a Levite: a member of the tribe of Levi, who served in the temple
decisions.reason: Levites helped the priests in the temple. The law gave Levi no share of the land (Numbers 18:20), but by this time Levites could own property (compare Jeremiah 32:7-9).

decisions.choice: a Cypriot by birth: from the Jewish community on the island of Cyprus
decisions.reason: Many Jews lived on Cyprus (11:19). Barnabas later goes there with Paul (13:4).

decisions.choice: now: an example of the giving just described
decisions.reason: Joseph is one example of 4:34-35. The next example, Ananias and Sapphira (5:1-11), is the opposite.

decisions.choice: One of them was; one of the believers was
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable show that Joseph is an example of what was just described.

decisions.choice: one who encourages
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the meaning of the name, as the meaning note explains; Literal keeps its form.

decisions.choice: gave it to the apostles
alternatives: laid it at the apostles' feet
decisions.reason: As at 4:35.
